minutes.headline: Finance Committee reorganized and heard a first read of a free cash policy change; vote set for next meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee elected its officers and assigned liaisons to town departments and committees. Members reviewed a first look at comparison spending data from nearby towns, and a draft revision to the free cash policy was presented for a first read. The town accountant reported a small increase in spending capacity from the state budget, and the calendar of fall meetings was set.

public_comment.topic: Followed up on Ashby paying for capital improvements through one year's tax bills rather than borrowing; Ashby has virtually no debt.
Asked how the five percent stabilization figure is calculated and whether debt or a special stabilization fund should be included in the base.
Urged paying down non-exempt debt rather than putting as much money away for rainy days.

votes.motion: Nominate Terry as chair of the committee
John to continue as vice chair
John Henshaw to represent the Finance Committee on the capital planning committee

budget_items.what_was_said: Lunenburg police spending was higher in the first year than the next, which was attributed to moving to regional dispatch.
Lunenburg fire spending exceeded Groton's by a large margin across the years compared.
Lunenburg education spending was stable one year and rose the next, placing it near the top of the comparison towns.
Draft revision drops pavement management as a free cash priority since it is funded elsewhere and directs free cash toward the OPEB trust fund and special purpose stabilization.

budget_items.topic: FY19 state budget cherry sheet change
budget_items.what_was_said: The state budget raised spending capacity slightly through cherry sheet and assessment changes; new growth is not yet certified.
figures_as_heard: one hundred and sixty two thousand one hundred and thirty three dollars

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill asbestos abatement state funding
budget_items.what_was_said: The state budget included money for Turkey Hill asbestos abatement, which can be reappropriated from the capital plan at a special town meeting.
A resident urged paying down non-exempt debt rather than building reserves.

decisions.decision: Next meeting is August 23; the chair expects the seventh Finance Committee member may be appointed that day.
The free cash policy recommendation will be placed on the next agenda for a vote to recommend to the Board of Selectmen.
Minutes from the July 26 meeting will go on the next agenda.
New growth and how to factor it into anticipated budgets will be added to the next agenda.
Meeting calendar set through December, with no meeting on November 22 for Thanksgiving; Tuesdays kept open for a possible special town meeting public hearing.
Liaisons assigned: Mark for public access cable, John for capital planning, George for Department of Public Works, John for police, George for fire, Jay for sewer and green communities.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard a first read of a draft free cash policy revision that drops pavement management as a priority and favors the OPEB trust and special purpose stabilization.
The free cash policy recommendation goes on the next agenda for a vote on whether to recommend it to the Board of Selectmen.
The committee elected officers, then assigned members as liaisons to departments and committees; John Henshaw was voted to the capital planning committee.
The town accountant said the state budget raised spending capacity slightly and included Turkey Hill asbestos abatement money that a special town meeting could reappropriate.
Members reviewed first comparison spending data from nearby towns for police, fire and education.

why_it_matters: The free cash policy steers where leftover town money goes, so a change toward reserves and the OPEB trust affects what is available to hold down future tax bills or fund projects.
The Turkey Hill abatement money could be reappropriated from the capital plan at a special town meeting, a vote residents may be asked to take.
